lessons.scriptText:
WRS LESSON PLAN - SUBSTEP 3.1
Group: Blue Group
Lesson 1
Reader 3 | Level AB

BLOCK 1 - Word Study

1. Sounds Quick Drill

Vowels: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ
Consonants: b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z
Welded/Glued and Exceptions: all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt
Prefixes Known: mid-, mis-, un-
Latin Bases Known: -fess-, -gress-, -mand-, -mit-, -pel-, -pend-, -press-, -rupt-, -sent-, -sist-, -stant-, -sult-, -tend-, -tent-, -vent-, -dict-, -duct-, -fect-, -flect-, -flict-, -ject-, -lect-, -pact-, -rect-, -sect-, -spect-, -struct-, -tact-, -tract-, -vict-
Suffixes Known: -s, -es

2. Teach & Review Concepts

a. Review Words / trouble spots
scraps, sprits, strath, sprint, strag, scramp

b. Current Words
muffin, publish, cobweb, nutmeg, mascot, picnic, cactus, napkin

3. Word Cards Activity

a. Review Word Cards
scraps, sprits, strath, sprint, strag, scramp
prefix: current pattern as assigned
suffix: current suffix pattern
Latin base: n/a

b. Current Word Cards
cactus, public, index, attic, mascot, muffin

4. Wordlist Reading (Independent)

Reader 3, page 2 (AB)
cactus, public, index, attic, mascot, muffin, rubbish, napkin, nutmeg, publish, rabbit, cobweb, picnic, metric, until
Goal: 12/15 for accuracy, 14/15 for fluency, 12/15 under 35 seconds for automaticity.

5. Sentence Reading

Use Reader 3, page 26 (AB).
High-frequency words: full, push, pulled, month, pushed, number, first, compound, words
My backpack was full of snacks.
I will push the mud back into the pigpen.
Sunfish are flat and long.
I will go for a long jog at sunup with Calvin.
Liz pulled the plant into the sunlit spot.
Did Bob get a suntan on his trip this month?
Ben pushed the catnip to the tomcat.
Devin had a small number of shellfish for lunch.
Did you slip in the bathtub?
At first, my laptop did not work well.


Extra page words for extension
tennis, hiccup, upset, goblin, tidbit, album, victim, discuss, shamrock

BLOCK 2 - Spelling

2. Teach & Review Concepts (Part 2)

cactus, mascot, napkin, nutmeg, cobweb

6. Quick Drill in Reverse

Say sounds for: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt

7. Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling

Read the base word first, add the suffix, then read and spell the complete word.

8. Dictation

Sounds
b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt

Words
cactus, mascot, napkin, nutmeg, cobweb

Phrases
full of shells
did pull back
pulled it off

Sentence
Dictation Book sentence source needed.

BLOCK 3 - Fluency / Comprehension

9. Controlled Passage

Use Reader 3, page 40 (AB) for the official passage.
Optional teacher-created quick passage using current charting words:
First, read cactus, public, and index.
Then read attic, mascot, and muffin.
Last, reread rubbish and napkin for accuracy.

10. Comprehension Question

What did the student need to read?

Teacher Move
start with sound tapping and oral blending before showing the word; use fewer first-read words and add a second accurate reread; use an assigned N page or review nonsense words only when they match the current substep pattern; Needs a smooth blend before sentence reading..

Group: Blue Group
Lesson 1
Reader 3 | Level AB

BLOCK 1 - Word Study

1. Sounds Quick Drill

Vowels: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ
Consonants: b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z
Welded/Glued and Exceptions: all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt
Prefixes Known: mid-, mis-, non-, tran-, trans-, un-, ab-, abs-, ad-, com-, con-, dis-, em-, en-, ex-, im-, in-, ob-, sub-
Latin Bases Known: -fess-, -gress-, -mand-, -mit-, -pel-, -pend-, -press-, -rupt-, -sent-, -sist-, -stant-, -sult-, -tend-, -tent-, -vent-, -dict-, -duct-, -fect-, -flect-, -flict-, -ject-, -lect-, -pact-, -rect-, -sect-, -spect-, -struct-, -tact-, -tract-, -vict-

2. Teach & Review Concepts

a. Review Words / trouble spots
expect, constrict, projects, insects, shiblent, tinzomp

b. Current Words
accredit, intellect, fantastic, exhibit, basketball, atlantic, establish, stepchildren

a. Review Word Cards
expect, constrict, projects, insects, shiblent, tinzomp
prefix: n/a
suffix: current suffix pattern
Latin base: n/a

b. Current Word Cards
establish, recommend, shipbottom, intellect, congressman, accustom

4. Wordlist Reading (Independent)

Reader 3, page 119 (AB)
establish, recommend, shipbottom, intellect, congressman, accustom, grandchildren, fantastic, basketball, wisconsin, exhibit, stepchildren, accomplish, accredit, atlantic
Goal: 12/15 for accuracy, 14/15 for fluency, 12/15 under 35 seconds for automaticity.

5. Sentence Reading

Use Reader 3, page 127 (AB).
High-frequency words: people, always, say, may, hour, today, syllable, division
The rocketship will have six people on it.
I always say that your sandwiches are fantastic!
Mr. and Mrs. Wilkinson are the people from Galveston, Texas.
I know that my penmanship is always the best in the class.
I may recommend Josh for the job.
Justin was at the fossil exhibit for over an hour.
Did you walk to Manhattan today?
After today, the new products will be on exhibit for the public to visit.
The congressman met with all the people on the list.
Today, we will establish the plan for the trip to the Atlantic.

lexington, congressmen

2. Teach & Review Concepts (Part 2)

establish, congressman, fantastic, basketball, exhibit

Read the base word first, add the suffix, then read and spell the complete word.

Sounds
b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt

establish, congressman, fantastic, basketball, exhibit

his big day
will come today
may not go

Sentence
Dad got a rocketship for the children.

BLOCK 3 - Fluency / Comprehension

9. Controlled Passage

Use Reader 3, page 136 (AB) for the official passage.
Optional teacher-created quick passage using current charting words:
First, read establish, recommend, and shipbottom.
Then read intellect, congressman, and accustom.
Last, reread grandchildren and fantastic for accuracy.

10. Comprehension Question

What did the student need to read?

start with sound tapping and oral blending before showing the word; use fewer first-read words and add a second accurate reread; use an assigned N page or review nonsense words only when they match the current substep pattern; Needs a smooth blend before sentence reading..

TEACH TODAY LESSON PLAN - SUBSTEP 2.1
Group: Group 4 - Ariana 2.1
Lesson 1
Reader 2 | Level AB

BLOCK 1 - Word Study

1. Sounds Quick Drill

Vowels: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ
Consonants: b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z
Welded/Glued and Exceptions: all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk
Prefixes Known: n/a
Latin Bases Known: n/a
Suffixes Known: -s, -es

2. Teach & Review Concepts

a. Review Words / trouble spots
fishes, kids, runs, checks, cheds, kigs

b. Current Words
sang, rung, bang, hung, gang, rang, king, ring

3. Word Cards Activity

a. Review Word Cards
fishes, kids, runs, checks, cheds, kigs
prefix: n/a
suffix: current suffix pattern
Latin base: n/a

b. Current Word Cards
long, song, rang, sing, thing, sang

4. Wordlist Reading (Independent)

Reader 2, page 2 (AB)
long, song, rang, sing, thing, sang, lung, wing, rung, hang, bang, king, gang, hung, ring
Goal: 12/15 for accuracy, 14/15 for fluency, 12/15 under 35 seconds for automaticity.

5. Sentence Reading

Use Reader 2, page 9 (AB).
High-frequency words: would, were, asked, her, who, should, could, now, how, ng
I would ring that bell at six.
Were you the one who sang that song?
Val asked Tim to get her a ring.
Ling got her ping pong balls back.
Ming let the cat on the back deck.
You should not bang on that tin box.
I asked the king for a job.
I could hang this long rod on the wall.
Will Kim sing her song now?
How does the king have such bad luck?


Extra page words for extension
link, rink, rank, think, sank, sink, honk, bank, dunk, tank

BLOCK 2 - Spelling

2. Teach & Review Concepts (Part 2)

long, song, rang, sing, thing

6. Quick Drill in Reverse

Say sounds for: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk

7. Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling

Read the base word first, add the suffix, then read and spell the complete word.

8. Dictation

Sounds
b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk

Words
long, song, rang, sing, thing

Phrases
her six cats
has her pup
at her job

Sentence
Ron rang the bell at one.

BLOCK 3 - Fluency / Comprehension

9. Controlled Passage

Use Reader 2, page 14 (AB) for the official passage.
Optional teacher-created quick passage using current charting words:
First, read long, song, and rang.
Then read sing, thing, and sang.
Last, reread lung and wing for accuracy.

10. Comprehension Question

What did the student need to read?

Teacher Move
Follow the standard routine for 2.1: review, teach, read, spell, then transfer to sentence and passage reading.

lesson.scriptText:
TEACH TODAY LESSON PLAN - SUBSTEP 2.1
Group: Demo Group
Lesson 1
Reader 2 | Level AB

BLOCK 1 - Word Study

1. Sounds Quick Drill

Vowels: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ
Consonants: b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z
Welded/Glued and Exceptions: all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk
Prefixes Known: n/a
Latin Bases Known: n/a
Suffixes Known: -s, -es

2. Teach & Review Concepts

a. Review Words / trouble spots
sacks, caps, quits, baths, zops, vibs

b. Current Words
sang, bang, hung, rang, sing, hang, ring, king

3. Word Cards Activity

a. Review Word Cards
sacks, caps, quits, baths, zops, vibs
prefix: n/a
suffix: current suffix pattern
Latin base: n/a

b. Current Word Cards
long, song, rang, sing, thing, sang

4. Wordlist Reading (Independent)

Reader 2, page 2 (AB)
long, song, rang, sing, thing, sang, lung, wing, rung, hang, bang, king, gang, hung, ring
Goal: 12/15 for accuracy, 14/15 for fluency, 12/15 under 35 seconds for automaticity.

5. Sentence Reading

Use Reader 2, page 9 (AB).
High-frequency words: would, were, asked, her, who, should, could, now, how, ng
I would ring that bell at six.
Were you the one who sang that song?
Val asked Tim to get her a ring.
Ling got her ping pong balls back.
Ming let the cat on the back deck.
You should not bang on that tin box.
I asked the king for a job.
I could hang this long rod on the wall.
Will Kim sing her song now?
How does the king have such bad luck?


Extra page words for extension
link, rink, rank, think, sank, sink, honk, bank, dunk, tank

BLOCK 2 - Spelling

2. Teach & Review Concepts (Part 2)

long, song, rang, sing, thing

6. Quick Drill in Reverse

Say sounds for: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk

7. Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling

Read the base word first, add the suffix, then read and spell the complete word.

8. Dictation

Sounds
b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk

Words
long, song, rang, sing, thing

Phrases
her six cats
has her pup
at her job

Sentence
Ron rang the bell at one.

BLOCK 3 - Fluency / Comprehension

9. Controlled Passage

Use Reader 2, page 14 (AB) for the official passage.
Optional teacher-created quick passage using current charting words:
First, read long, song, and rang.
Then read sing, thing, and sang.
Last, reread lung and wing for accuracy.

10. Comprehension Question

What did the student need to read?

Teacher Move
Follow the standard routine for 2.1: review, teach, read, spell, then transfer to sentence and passage reading.

Group: Demo Group
Lesson 1
Reader 3 | Level AB

BLOCK 1 - Word Study

1. Sounds Quick Drill

Vowels: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ
Consonants: b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z
Welded/Glued and Exceptions: all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt
Prefixes Known: mid-, mis-, non-, tran-, trans-, un-, ab-, abs-, ad-, com-, con-, dis-, em-, en-, ex-, im-, in-, ob-, sub-
Latin Bases Known: -fess-, -gress-, -mand-, -mit-, -pel-, -pend-, -press-, -rupt-, -sent-, -sist-, -stant-, -sult-, -tend-, -tent-, -vent-, -dict-, -duct-, -fect-, -flect-, -flict-, -ject-, -lect-, -pact-, -rect-, -sect-, -spect-, -struct-, -tact-, -tract-, -vict-
Suffixes Known: -s, -es, -ed, -ing

2. Teach & Review Concepts

a. Review Words / trouble spots
misconnect, nonfossil, shipbottom, disestablish, stodlim, drappog

b. Current Words
testing, helping, ended, willing, holding, thinking, telling, planting

3. Word Cards Activity

a. Review Word Cards
misconnect, nonfossil, shipbottom, disestablish, stodlim, drappog
prefix: n/a
suffix: current suffix pattern
Latin base: n/a

b. Current Word Cards
willing, landed, holding, testing, shifting, planting

4. Wordlist Reading (Independent)

Reader 3, page 142 (AB)
willing, landed, holding, testing, shifting, planting, spelling, filling, thinking, listed, resting, ended, telling, helping, checking
Goal: 12/15 for accuracy, 14/15 for fluency, 12/15 under 35 seconds for automaticity.

5. Sentence Reading

Use Reader 3, page 151 (AB).
High-frequency words: throughout, great, called, through, need
Kim is checking her backpack for another pen.
Ross was stacking blocks when they fell on him.
Throughout the trip, the children kept asking to visit the king.
Megan bonded with her new pet cat.
The ship will be docking at our next stop by sunset.
I am thinking that it would be great if we called Gram today.
We are through with the rented tents.
People must stop dumping trash in the lot.
Do you need help lifting this very big lamp?
Are you filling the fishpond with water today?


Extra page words for extension
drafting, rested, asking, acting, fishing, funded, planted, bringing, rushing, wishing

BLOCK 2 - Spelling

2. Teach & Review Concepts (Part 2)

landed, holding, testing, shifting, planting

6. Quick Drill in Reverse

Say sounds for: short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt

7. Teach & Review Concepts for Spelling

Read the base word first, add the suffix, then read and spell the complete word.

8. Dictation

Sounds
b, c, ch, ck, d, f, g, h, j, k, l, m, n, p, qu, r, s, sh, t, th, v, w, wh, x, y, z; short vowels: ă, ĕ, ĭ, ŏ, ŭ; all, am, an, ang, ing, ong, ung, ank, ink, onk, unk, ild, ind, old, ost, olt

Words
landed, holding, testing, shifting, planting

Phrases
through the mud
through the day
not through yet

Sentence
Brad shifted the plant into the sun.

BLOCK 3 - Fluency / Comprehension

9. Controlled Passage

Use Reader 3, page 156 (AB) for the official passage.
Optional teacher-created quick passage using current charting words:
First, read willing, landed, and holding.
Then read testing, shifting, and planting.
Last, reread spelling and filling for accuracy.

10. Comprehension Question

What did the student need to read?

Teacher Move
I'm not sure what to do with. Xavier, he night need more practice. so the students are doing OK but they probably are practice on this lesson again. Let’s focus on those ING ANG ONG UNG sounds..
